title: Panel membership visible in the scenario trace (#3 prefactor)
description:
Make the Panel's membership visible in the scenario trace, so the Conformance Suite can see a
Reviewer that was never spawned. Pure prefactor for #3: no requirement changes, the suite stays
green, and the enumeration does not grow.

## Why

`observed_trace()` in `conformance/run` (lines 46–68) reconstructs `panel<r>:<class>` by counting
only the Reviewers that recorded a run, so three-spawned-three-ok renders as `panel<r>:all`,
byte-identical to four. The formal side has the same hole: `tools/formal/Rloop/Loop.lean:95`
makes the Panel a single `Spawn` constructor carrying a `Panel` class, and `Scenarios.lean:74`
renders it `s!"panel{r}:{panelName p}"` — there is nowhere to record *which* Reviewers ran.

**All 206 committed scenarios would stay green over an Implementation that silently ran three
Reviewers.** Same class as the CodeRabbit finding on #2.

This contradicts #3's settled comment, which said the Lean model needs no change. That is true of
the decision function and wrong about the trace, where the Suite's coverage actually lives — see
the correction comment on #3 (2026-09-20T21:28:04Z). `tools/formal/` is in scope.

## What to change

- `Spawn.panel` carries the membership.
- The render in `Scenarios.lean` emits it.
- `python3 tools/check_scenarios.py --write` rewrites all 206 rows with the longer trace token;
  commit what it writes (`AGENTS.md`: the scenarios file is rendered, not hand-kept).
- `observed_trace()` in `conformance/run` is taught to match.

## Why it does not grow the enumeration

Under today's requirements every Panel is the same four Reviewers, so membership is a constant.
The alphabet is unchanged; only the token is longer. Availability as an *axis* is a different
job and belongs with the requirement change — see the availability-scenario-axis ticket.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `conformance/scenarios.tsv` still has 206 rows, each with membership in the trace column.
- A fake scripted to skip one Reviewer **fails** a scenario that expects four. It does not today;
  that failure is the whole point of this ticket and must be demonstrated, not asserted.
- No requirement text changes. `git diff` touches only `tools/formal/`, `tools/`-written files
  and `conformance/`.

## Lands next to

`F4` ("The scenario alphabet is a choice"), whose closing line now has a sibling case: an
Implementation that passes the suite while running a three-Reviewer Panel.
close_reason: Accepted after Round 2: Panel membership is rendered and observed, timed-out Reviewers remain members, 206 scenarios preserved, omission controls S2/S38 reject skipped sol, all six gates and executable conformance with self-check pass.

title: Specify the model-availability probe and the fail-open rule (#3)
description:
Specify the model-availability probe: its command lines, when it runs, and the fail-open rule.
The first half of #3. Nothing changes about what rloop does with the answer — that is the
record-omitted-reviewer ticket.

## Why

An exhausted model does not fail fast. It hangs, writes zero bytes on both streams, and is killed
at its seat's timeout. A Reviewer seat pays `--reviewer-timeout` (1800s default) **every Round**
for a model that was never going to answer.

Verified 2026-09-20: `claude -p "/usage"` exits 0 in seconds and reports per-family limits with
reset times, and answers just as fast *through* the exhausted model, so one call covers every
claude family. codex exposes no quota at all; both codex seats share one ChatGPT account, so a
tiny `codex exec` call is the only direct probe and one probe covers both.

## Settled already (#3, do not re-derive)

- **The check runs immediately before the Panel, never at Run start.** `astra` and `sol` produced
  the same counterexample independently: an Implementer call may run for hours past a quota reset,
  so evidence gathered at Run start can suppress a Reviewer that would have answered.
- **Fail open.** Unknown availability, a probe that fails, output that does not parse, or an
  unrecognised model name MUST spawn the Reviewer normally. Only positively recognised, unexpired
  exhaustion may short-circuit.
- **Remove only, never substitute.** Substitution silently changes which model judged the work.
- **The parser lives in this Specification.** The "language-neutral" objection is answered in #3
  point 7: this set is language-neutral about the *Implementation* (`ADR-0001`) and is
  deliberately harness-specific everywhere else — it already hardcodes the model names, the
  `--effort` values and the deny list byte for byte, and `AGT-17` pins the CLI versions.

## What to change

- A new requirement for the probe's command lines, stated verbatim like every other
  (`ADR-0001`, `OVR-2`), with `tools/check_fixtures.py --write` regenerating the fixtures. Never
  edit `conformance/fixtures/` by hand.
- **Narrow `OVR-1`**, which forbids the probe as written: *"It MUST NOT parse a Reviewer's
  output, an Implementer's output, or any part of the Finished File beyond its first line."* A
  quota probe is rloop parsing a model CLI's output and acting on it. Follow `F9`'s six-day-old
  precedent exactly: it narrowed `DIR-4`'s "entire and *unparsed*" to "entire and *unmodified*"
  to admit one datum. This is the second instance of that pattern.
- `AGT-17`: record the CLI versions the `/usage` format was verified against. `AGT-17` already
  concedes this risk class — *"a flag that a newer CLI rejects is found only by a live Run"* — so
  a drifted format is not a new kind of exposure, and fail-open degrades it to doing nothing.
- `CNF` items in `06-conformance.md` for the three fail-open paths: probe fails, probe output
  does not parse, unrecognised model name. Distinguish exhaustion from a typo: verified,
  `claude -p "say hi" --model claude-bogus-9` exits 1 in seconds with
  `[claude-code:unrecognized_model]`, while exhaustion hangs with zero bytes.

## ADR

**`ADR-0006`**, not `ADR-0005`. #3's settled comment reserved 0005, and 0005 was taken on
2026-09-21 by "The operator's view has one home and Implementations point at it". Check
`docs/adr/` for the next free number before writing, not this ticket.

Subject: rloop reads a vendor's human-facing quota report and fails open. Hard to reverse,
surprising without context, and argued against by all three advisers — record what they said and
why it was overridden.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `grep` finds the probe's command line in exactly one document, and its fixture is generated.
- Every new requirement is cited by a `CNF` item. The coverage gate holds at zero with no ratchet
  baseline, so an excuse-table entry is not available here — and would be false, since #3's
  Testability section says all of this is black-box testable.
close_reason: AGT-18, RUN-21, ADR-0006; OVR-1 narrowed per F9, OVR-2/RUN-7/AGT-1/AGT-13 amended, DIR-4 rows, CNF-24-26 with implementations and a probe role in the fake. Six gates exit 0. Suite is 20/4 against rloop-bash: CNF-9/24/25/26 red until it implements the probe, which is ADR-0001's designed path.

title: Record an unavailable Reviewer in place, never drop it (#3)
description:
An unavailable Reviewer stays in the Panel and is recorded as not having run, rather than being
dropped so the Panel runs with three. The second half of #3, and the part that changes behaviour.

Depends on the availability-probe ticket: fail-open means unknown availability MUST spawn
normally, so without a probe command line this arm is unreachable in a live Run and unscriptable
in the Suite — there is nothing for a fake to answer.

## Settled already (#3, do not re-derive)

- **Record, do not drop.** Consequence: there is no Panel floor to choose. `RUN-15` already fixes
  one — one survivor is enough, zero is exit 2 — and no version of this change alters it.
  Question 1 of #3 is withdrawn.
- **"Did not run" counts toward `RUN-15`'s zero-survivor abort.** An account wholly out of quota
  therefore loses the Round: the Implementer may have run for hours and committed work, and rloop
  exits 2 with no judge and no Finished File. Accepted unchanged — four timeouts reach the
  identical exit today, two hours later, and `F10` already rejected having rloop author a
  `finished.md` of its own for precisely this case.
- **A distinct literal is required.** `REVIEWER FAILED (exit <status>)` cannot describe a call
  that never happened — there is no status — and `PRM-2` tells the Manager that line means
  `crashed or timed out`. Reusing it makes both passages false and costs the Manager the
  distinction `RUN-15`'s own rationale rests on: *"One Reviewer down is a degraded Panel the
  Manager can weigh; four down is a broken environment."*
- **No new noun.** A `Seat`/occupant split was proposed and withdrawn by its own proposer.

## What to change

- `RUN-15`: a third arm for the omitted call, and which failures count toward the abort.
- `RUN-7` §3 — *"all four Reviewer calls … started concurrently and all waited for"* — goes
  false. Amend it.
- `RUN-8`.
- `PRM-2`: the distinct literal. Amended either way, per the settled comment.
- `DIR-4`: the Feedback File's authorship when rloop writes it in the Reviewer's place, and an
  absent or empty `.err`.
- `CONTEXT.md`: the two glossary entries drafted in #3 land **here**, not earlier — the Feedback
  File entry cites a `RUN-15` clause that does not exist until this ticket.

  ```
  **Panel**:
  The **Reviewers** `AGT-11` designates for one **Round**, each a different model, run side by
  side.

  **Feedback File**:
  One **Reviewer**'s findings for one **Round**, written for the **Manager**; rloop writes it in
  the Reviewer's place when the call failed or was never made (`RUN-15`).
  _Avoid_: Review, findings file
  ```

- `PRM-4` does **not** change. `PRM-6` forbids conditional text, and "one of four independent
  Reviewers" stays true of a designated roster.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- All four unavailable exits 2 with no judge spawned and no Finished File — **instantly**, not
  after four timeouts. This is `RUN-15`'s existing rule firing on the new arm, not separate
  behaviour, which is why it has no ticket of its own.
- The Manager can tell "did not run" from "crashed or timed out" by reading the Feedback File
  alone. Grep `PRM-2` for both literals.
- Before writing that a clause landed, `grep` for its identifier. A decision gets its identifier
  when it is accepted (`AGENTS.md`).
close_reason: RUN-15 third arm + zero-survivor counting both kinds of down; RUN-7/RUN-8/DIR-4/PRM-2/CONTEXT.md amended; CNF-27 added incl. the mixed abort case. Six gates exit 0; suite 18/7 against rloop-bash (CNF-11/12 join the reds because PRM-2 changed). F13 records that the Lean pair proves the failure arm only. 'All four unavailable' is unreachable - no codex probe - and RUN-15 is left unscoped because mixed down states are reachable.

title: Availability as a scenario axis: the six cases (#3)
description:
Add availability as an axis in the scenario alphabet and generate the six cases #3 requires
before any of this is trusted. This is the ticket that grows the enumeration.

Depends on the panel-membership-in-trace ticket (the trace needs somewhere to put membership) and
on the record-omitted-reviewer ticket (the behaviour has to exist to be enumerated).

## Why separate from the prefactor

Making membership visible does not grow the alphabet: under today's requirements every Panel is
the same four Reviewers, so membership is a constant. Enumerating *availability* multiplies the
generated set, so it belongs with the requirement change rather than with the mechanical
rewrite. Splitting them keeps a 206-row regeneration reviewable on its own.

## The six cases, from #3

1. One Reviewer unavailable — recorded, not spawned; the Run continues with the rest.
2. All four unavailable — exit 2, no judge spawned, no Finished File.
3. A Reviewer re-admitted in a later Round, once the fake reports capacity again.
4. A probe that fails — fail open, the Reviewer is spawned.
5. A probe whose output does not parse — fail open, the Reviewer is spawned.
6. An unrecognised model name — fail open and loud, not a silently smaller Panel.

Cases 4–6 are the fail-open paths. They are the ones that make the rule falsifiable; without
them "fail open" is a sentence nobody can check.

## What to change

- Availability as an axis in `tools/formal/Rloop/Scenarios.lean`'s alphabet.
- `python3 tools/check_scenarios.py --write`, then commit what it writes.
- The fakes in `conformance/` gain a way to report exhaustion and to report capacity again.
- `conformance/scenarios.tsv`.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- Each of the six cases fails against an Implementation that gets it wrong. Demonstrate the
  failure for each; a scenario that passes both ways tests nothing. This is the lesson `F5`
  already paid for — *"a check and its subject built from one misreading agree with each other"*.
- The row count grows, and the growth is reported in the commit message with the before and
  after.

## Lands next to

`F4` ("The scenario alphabet is a choice"). If this materially multiplies the set, say so in
`F4` — it is the finding that owns the size of the enumeration.

Case 2 is the reachable mixed form (RUN-21 gives no codex model a family). All eight mutants of rloop-bash go red after the same lines pass unmutated. title: PRM-4's clean-path shortcut swallows item 0 (#4)
description:
`PRM-4`'s report block contradicts itself on the clean path, and the contradiction is why a codex
Reviewer's bare `No findings.` carries no provenance. Fix the prompt; no vendor reasoning needed.

## The defect

Item 0 says *"Say 'I ran everything I needed' if that is true"*. The block then ends:

```
If there is nothing to report, write exactly: No findings.
```

`write exactly` names a literal, and it is the last and most specific instruction in the block. A
Reviewer with nothing to report is being told to emit that string and nothing else. The codex
Reviewers comply; `opus` is the one deviating by adding item 0 on top.

Evidence is on rloop-spec#4 (2026-09-21 comment): across seven Run Directories every bare report
is **exactly 13 bytes**, and every codex Reviewer that was itself blocked wrote item 0 in full —
including `sol`, which #4's original text reports as never complying.

## The change

In `03-prompts.md`, `PRM-4`, replace the closing line of the report block with:

```
If you have nothing for items 1 and 2, write item 0 and then exactly: No findings.
```

Keeps the literal that makes a clean report machine-recognisable; stops it swallowing item 0.

Then `python3 tools/check_fixtures.py --write`. Never edit `conformance/fixtures/` by hand
(`AGENTS.md`). A prompt is changed in `03-prompts.md` and nowhere else.

## What follows in the Implementation

`PRM-4`'s bytes are normative (`OVR-2`), so `rloop-bash` changes its hardcoded prompt and bumps
its `spec/` pin, then `spec/conformance/run ./result/bin/rloop` must pass. That is `ADR-0001`'s
designed path, not an accident of it. `CNF-11`/`CNF-12` compare the hardcoded prompt to the
fixtures byte for byte, so a missed byte fails the suite rather than going live.

## What does not change

`conformance/run` lines 164 and 320 compare a Feedback File to `"No findings."` exactly, but those
are **fake** Reviewers' canned outputs testing rloop's pass-through plumbing. A fake does not read
a prompt. Leave them.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `grep -n "No findings" 03-prompts.md` shows the literal in exactly one place, inside the new
  sentence.
- The regenerated fixture for `PRM-4` matches the document; `check_fixtures.py` proves it.
- In `rloop-bash`: `spec/conformance/run ./result/bin/rloop` passes against the bumped pin.

## Verification is a live observation, not a suite item

Only a live Run shows whether the reworded block is followed — the Suite proves the prompt was
*sent*, never that a model obeyed it (`00-overview.md`, *How much to trust this*). Record it as a
`CNF-22` observation with the next release, against a specific prediction: **a clean codex report
carries item 0 and the literal both.** If it still emits 13 bytes, the cause was not the shortcut
and #4's option 2 — telling the Manager in `PRM-2` to weigh a report with no item 0 — is next.
close_reason: Accepted exact PRM-4 amendment and regenerated fixture in Round 1; Manager verified byte preservation and all specification gates PASS. Remaining Implementation adoption tracked in rl-bvz; live observation tracked in rl-vgy.

title: Restatement check plus the ported citation gate (F2, #11)
description:
Catch a rule restated outside its home. `F2`'s trigger fired: one pull request produced eight
findings of one rule living in more than one place, in a set of 102 requirements that six gates
call green. Decided 2026-09-21 on rloop-spec#11; `F2` records the decision.

## Two parts, and they compose

**1. The restatement check, in `tools/check_ids.py`.** That file already parses every requirement
definition (`DEF_RE`) and every citation (`CITE_RE`) across the root documents and the ADRs, so
this is an addition to an existing pass, not a new gate:

> A line that cites another requirement's identifier while carrying an RFC-2119 keyword of its own
> must either be that requirement's own definition, or carry the owner's words verbatim in
> backticks.

The verbatim-quote exemption is not a new concession — `AGENTS.md` already demands it: *"**Quote
the sentence.** A claim about what another requirement says carries that requirement's own words
in backticks."*

**Probed 2026-09-21: 8 lines in the whole set.** Reviewable in one sitting. Two of them
(`01-run-lifecycle.md:221`, `03-prompts.md:112`) already quote and clear themselves. At least one
is a real second normative copy: `01-run-lifecycle.md:23` — *"A lone Run MAY start on a dirty
tree; a Run inside a Sequence MUST NOT (`SEQ-4`)"* — states `SEQ-4`'s rule itself while citing it.
Triage all eight; each is either the home, a quote, or a defect.

**2. Port `check_citations.py` from provisiond-spec.** It is at
`~/projects/provisiond-spec/tools/check_citations.py`, 284 lines, with a `citation-baseline.json`
alongside it. It flags a quoted phrase attributed to a requirement whose body does not contain it
— which is exactly what makes part 1's escape hatch real rather than honour-system. Without it a
writer can claim to quote and be wrong, which is how drift instances 1 and 4 survived
`check_fixtures.py`: the fixture faithfully reproduced the wrong sentence.

Wire both into `tools/check-all.sh`, each exit code captured directly, never through a pipe.

## Deliberately not done

`check_obligations.py` stays deferred, recorded in `F2`. Of the eight instances the one obligation
finding was a paraphrase, not a duty assigned to another requirement's subject. Build it when an
instance of that shape appears.

## Two of #11's four shapes need nothing

Recorded so they are not rebuilt:

- **In an Implementation repository.** `rloop-bash`'s copy was deleted for a pointer
  (`ADR-0005`, douglaz/rloop-bash#7). Nothing left to drift, and no check in this repository could
  reach it anyway.
- **In non-normative prose.** `CONTEXT.md`'s example dialogue now uses no value this Specification
  owns — no identifier, no filename, no exit status. A survey of every example dialogue in the
  author's repositories found nine, of which rloop's was the only one naming a spec-owned filename
  and the only one restating identified requirements; the other eight already followed the
  convention with no rule and no gate. There is nothing systemic here to enforce.

What remains is shape 1, across files — which is the shape a machine can find, because both ends
name an identifier. Shape 2, a requirement contradicting itself internally, has no mechanical
catch and stays a review duty.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, with every gate in
  `README.md`'s *Gates* table passing — the existing identifiers gate now carrying the
  restatement check, and the ported citation gate added beside it. *This read "eight gates"
  until 2026-09-22 and was wrong twice over: six plus one is seven, and a count written into
  prose is what `AGENTS.md`'s "Cite the list; let it hold the number" forbids. A Manager
  blocked the Run on the contradiction rather than choosing a reading (`RUN-19`).*
- The restatement check fails on a deliberately introduced second normative copy, and passes once
  that copy quotes its owner. Demonstrate both directions; a check that only ever passes tests
  nothing (`F5`).
- `check_citations.py` fails on a quote altered by one word. Demonstrate it.
- Every one of the eight lines flagged today is triaged: home, quote, or fixed.
close_reason: Accepted after Round 4: restatement and owner-only citation checks integrated; original probe triaged; all README gates and 41 citation controls pass. Formatting-normalization precision recorded separately; existing lexical limits accepted.

title: Probe shapes RUN-21 rules on and the suite never produces
description:
Two shapes of probe output `RUN-21` gives a rule for, and `conformance/run` never produces. Both
were found by reviewers reading `RUN-21` against `conformance/fakes/agent`, not by a red item —
the suite is green over them because the fake cannot express them.

## The two cases

1. **The aggregate line at 100%.** The fake's `clear` shape always writes
   `Current week (all models): 67% used`, and the `fable`/`opus` shapes write it at 67% too. So
   `Current week (all models): 100% used` — the likeliest real exhaustion, a whole account out —
   is never seen. `RUN-21` says it reads `unknown`, deliberately: *"no family is named in it,
   nobody has observed what the probe prints when a whole account is exhausted, and a rule written
   against an unobserved format is a guess."* That is a rule, and nothing tests it.

2. **Both families at 100% at once.** `fable` and `opus` are scripted one at a time. Two
   `unavailable` Reviewers in one Round is reachable in the real world the moment an account's
   Fable and Opus buckets are both spent, and it exercises what one family cannot: two Reviewers
   not called, `astra` and `sol` still called, `failed` reaching 2 and the Run still reaching its
   judge.

## What to change

- `conformance/fakes/agent`: an `aggregate` shape writing `Current week (all models): 100% used`,
  and a `both` shape writing Fable and Opus at 100% in one output.
- `CNF-26`: add the aggregate shape to its list of readings that leave every Reviewer `unknown`.
- `CNF-27`: add the two-unavailable case — `fable` and `opus` neither called and both recorded,
  `astra` and `sol` both called, the judge reached, the Run ending 0.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all gates PASS.
- Each new case fails against an Implementation that gets it wrong. Demonstrate both; a case that
  passes either way is what this ticket exists to remove.
- `spec/conformance/run ./result/bin/rloop --self-check` still passes against `rloop-bash`, which
  already handles both correctly — so these are coverage, not a behaviour change. If either goes
  red, the Implementation was wrong and the ticket found a real defect.
close_reason: Accepted Round 1: aggregate and both Probe shapes covered; gates pass, conformance 25/25 with self-check; aggregate mutant fails only CNF-26 and both-family mutant fails only CNF-27. Line-termination follow-up rl-vcq.

title: Clarify ownership of line termination in Probe and not-run records
description:
Follow-up from Opus suggestions 1 and 2 in Round 1 of Run 20260921T212700.418216043Z-2328148, reviewing rl-probe-uncovered-shapes-gp1.

The existing CNF-27 Feedback File comparison requires a terminating newline and rejects extra blank lines; the accepted coverage task explicitly preserved that convention. Its amended prose now makes the newline explicit. RUN-15 says `holding exactly` followed by `REVIEWER NOT RUN (unavailable)` and `and nothing else`, without explicitly describing the file terminator. Separately, CNF-27 compares probe-1.md byte for byte while CNF-25 and CNF-26 use command substitution, which strips trailing newlines.

Ask the Specification owner to settle the intended byte contract: whether a final newline is required, optional, or otherwise constrained for these records. title: Split the gates into a blocking and an advisory tier (ADR-0007)
description:
Split the restatement and citation gates into a blocking tier and an advisory tier, as
`ADR-0007` decides, and state in `F2` which tier each form belongs to.

`ADR-0007` is the decision and owns the reasoning. This bead is the work.

## What blocks the build

Exactly these forms, where the ownership claim is explicit in the syntax rather than inferred:

**Every introducer form below binds only an adjacent quotation** — nothing but whitespace
between the introducer and the quote. This applies to forms 1 and 2 exactly as to form 3.
Intervening prose makes the attribution advisory, whatever punctuation introduced it
(`ADR-0007`).

1. an identifier followed by a colon;
2. a possessive — `` `RUN-16`'s `` ;
3. a quotation immediately after its introducer;
4. a parenthetical whose **ownership prefix** is identifiers and separators. The ownership
   prefix is the content before the explanatory marker `F2` already recognises, or the whole
   content when there is none. So `` (`RUN-16`, `SEQ-4`) `` blocks, and
   `` (`SEQ-4`; but see `RUN-16` …) `` blocks on `SEQ-4` while the words after the marker claim
   nothing — which is why the acceptance table below gives that sentence the blocking tier.
   Do **not** test the whole parenthetical content; that would make the second advisory and
   contradict the table.

**The enumerated introducing-phrase list starts empty.** `ADR-0007` allows such a list; adding a
phrase to it is a separate decision recorded in `F2`, not part of this work. Do not invent
members for it.

## What warns and does not block

Everything else the current scanner detects, including ownership inferred across unrestricted
intervening prose. It still runs and still reports; it does not fail the build.

A finding in this tier must be distinguishable from a blocking one in the output, and the
aggregate runner's exit status must not depend on it.

## Also required

- **Restore `docs/adr/0006-*.md`'s original wording**, `` the probe `AGT-18` states ``, replacing
  `` the probe from `AGT-18` ``. It was changed in `2e7dfb8` only to stop a gate objecting to
  correct prose. Confirm it is silent or advisory afterwards, never blocking.
- Check the rest of the Specification for sentences reworded for the same reason and restore any
  found. `2e7dfb8` is the commit to read.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, with every gate in
  `README.md`'s Gates table passing.
- **Each of the four blocking forms has a control that fails when the attribution is false and
  passes when it is true.** Both directions, or the control proves nothing.
- **Each advisory form has a control asserting the behaviour that actually occurs** — the finding
  is reported and the exit status is unaffected. *Do not write a control asserting silence.*
  Closing one recognition route can re-open another: excluding a parenthetical from the citation
  route was measured to produce a `RESTATEMENT` finding instead, because `tools/check_ids.py`
  treats a span as covered only when an owner was found for it. Assert what happens.
- **A control covers the nearest-citation fallback** in `tools/spec_text.py`: a form the explicit
  recogniser declines can still be caught by that route, and the tier it lands in must be
  asserted, not assumed.
- These sentences, run through both gates, land in the tier `ADR-0007` gives them — verify each,
  and keep them as controls:

  | sentence | tier |
  |---|---|
  | `` `SEQ-4` says the rule is `<RUN-16's exact words>` (`RUN-16`). `` | advisory |
  | `` `SEQ-4` says nothing about `one session` (`RUN-16`). `` | advisory |
  | `` `<RUN-16's exact words>` (`SEQ-4`; but see `RUN-16` …). `` | blocking |
  | `` `<RUN-16's exact words>` (`RUN-16`, `SEQ-4`). `` | blocking |
  | `ADR-0006`'s restored sentence | not blocking |

- `F2` states which tier each form belongs to and points at `ADR-0007` for why. It does not
  restate the reasoning.
- `README.md`'s Gates table says which gates can fail the build and which only report.

## Not in scope

Teaching the scanner to parse relative clauses or any grammar beyond the four blocking forms.
Adding members to the enumerated introducing-phrase list. Narrowing the quotation-shape heuristic
on the inferred route — worth doing for advisory noise, but it is not this decision and
`ADR-0007` records why.

title: Refuse a Run whose Seat cannot answer (#3, ADR-0008)
description:
Refuse a Run whose Seat cannot answer, and catch a Manager that runs out mid-Run.

`ADR-0008` is the decision and owns the reasoning. This bead is the work. `CONTEXT.md` already
defines `Seat`; do not redefine it.

## What to change

**Amend `RUN-21`.** The Probe runs before the pick as well as immediately before each Round's
Panel. It records one `<seat>:<verdict>` line per Seat — `manager`, `implementer`, `fable`,
`opus`, `astra`, `sol`, in that order — in `probe-pick.md` before the pick and in `probe-<r>.md`
each Round. The verdict rule does not change: a Seat is `unavailable` only on the anchored
`Current week (<family>): 100% used` match with the family in the existing two-row table, and
`unknown` in every other case. A Seat whose model is outside that table is always `unknown`.

**Add `RUN-22`.** Two rules:

1. When `probe-pick.md` records the Manager's Seat `unavailable`, or the Implementer's Seat
   `unavailable`, rloop MUST exit 2 without spawning any agent, and MUST write to standard error a
   message naming the Seat, its model, and the reset the probe reported.
2. rloop MUST NOT make Round `r`'s judge call when `probe-<r>.md` records the Manager's Seat
   `unavailable`; it MUST exit 2. This precedes `RUN-11` rather than adding a row to it: that
   requirement decides `After every Manager call`, and a call that was never made is not one.

**Amend `DIR-4`.** Add `probe-pick.out`, `probe-pick.err` and `probe-pick.md`, written by rloop
before the pick. Restate `probe-<r>.md`'s entry as the per-Seat line.

**Amend `CONTEXT.md`'s `Probe` entry.** It scopes the Probe to a Round's Panel and to Reviewers;
both become false. Remove `preflight` from its avoided aliases — `ADR-0008` records why.

**The byte contract, already settled — do not treat it as open.** Every line of `probe-pick.md`
and `probe-<r>.md` ends with a newline, including the last, and a not-run Feedback File is
`REVIEWER NOT RUN (unavailable)` followed by a newline. `RUN-15`'s `and nothing else` means no
other content, not the absence of a terminator; say so where it is read. This is what rloop-bash
already writes — a not-run Feedback File measured 31 bytes on 2026-09-22 — so the change is to the
Specification and the items below, not to the Implementation. `CNF-25`, `CNF-26` and `CNF-27`
disagree about it today: one compares bytes, two use command substitution, which cannot see a
trailing newline. Align all three. This closes `rl-vcq`.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, every gate in `README.md`'s
  Gates table PASS.
- A conformance item for each of the two refusals, the Manager's Seat and the Implementer's Seat.
  **Each MUST assert that no agent was spawned**, not merely that the status was 2 — a Run that
  spawned a Manager and failed also exits 2, so a status-only check passes against an
  Implementation that ignores this entirely.
- A conformance item for the judge guard: a Run whose Round 2 probe records the Manager's Seat
  `unavailable` exits 2 with no `manager-judge-2.out` in the Run Directory.
- A control that a Seat whose model is outside the family table starts the Run, recorded
  `unknown`. Fail-open is unchanged, and this is what proves it.
- Every item above fails against an Implementation that gets it wrong. Demonstrate the failure for
  each; an item that passes both ways tests nothing (`F5`).
- `CNF-24`–`CNF-27` updated to the per-Seat record and passing.

## Not in scope

Substituting a model for an unavailable Seat, under any flag — `ADR-0008` rejects it. A second
Probe guarding the Implementer on every Round; `ADR-0008` records it as available on its own merits
and not this decision. Validating a model name against a roster: a typo still hangs, and nothing
here decides it.

**Do not add a pick-time refusal for an empty Panel.** Four `unavailable` Reviewer verdicts are
unreachable — two of the four Reviewers are codex and the family table holds no codex model, so
they always read `unknown`. `ADR-0008` records why the arm was dropped, and `RUN-15` keeps the

title: The fake and the model disagree past a probe script's last shape
description:
The fake and the model disagree about what the probe prints in a Round past the last shape a probe
script names. Today nothing reaches that Round, so this is a trap for the next probe script rather
than a live defect; found by the Panel on Run `20260922T214422.432717855Z-3306563`.

Pick one and make it so the other cannot drift:

- the fake falls through to `clear` rather than repeating the last shape, matching the model; or
- `probeReads`'s docstring (or the enumeration itself) states that a probe script MUST name a shape
  for every Round its cap allows, and something enforces it.

**Amend `RUN-20`.** An adviser whose model the relevant Probe recorded `unavailable` MUST be
treated as not having answered, without being called, and replaced by its counterpart under the

**Regenerate the argv fixtures** with `python3 tools/check_fixtures.py --write`. Never edit

**Extend the conformance items** that compare the Implementer's argument list so they see the new

the Implementer's argv.

title: gates.yml: nix flake check -L, and the README Gates section names the sandboxed run
description:
Two nits from the rl-flake-check-env-shebang-ur8 Panel (Run 20260923T061017.334217178Z-505649, commits 902e9ae and 3a3c919), neither a defect.

1. The new last step of .github/workflows/gates.yml runs 'nix flake check' without -L. On a red build Nix prints only 'Last 25 log lines'; panel-trace is the last gate so today's known red would survive the cut, but an earlier gate's diagnostic would be scrolled off by check-all.sh's SUMMARY table, in a set whose own gate writes 'a line no CI log hides'. Adding -L prints the derivation's full log. Optionally '--option sandbox true' pins the property the step's comment claims, should cachix/install-nix-action ever stop leaving the Linux default on.

2. README.md, Gates section ('CI runs the same script on every push'): still true, but it is now the one reader-facing place that does not say CI also builds the sandboxed derivation (flake.nix checks.gates). One clause closes it.

Acceptance: gates.yml step reads 'nix flake check -L'; README's Gates section mentions the sandboxed run in a sentence; nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh exits 0 unpiped.

title: CNF-29's not_named reads the whole stderr, which RUN-10 leaves unconstrained
description:
`CNF-29`'s `not_named` assertion reads the whole of standard error, which `RUN-10` leaves unconstrained.

Found by the opus Reviewer in Round 1 of the Run on `rl-seat-items-hygiene-a5t` (Run Directory
`20260923T062347.389579851Z-505649`); the judge call of that Round was lost at its bound, so this
is filed by hand from the review.

`conformance/run`'s `not_named` (near line 561) asserts that the word `manager` appears nowhere on
standard error in `CNF-29`'s two Runs, and `06-conformance.md` says so in prose: `In neither Run
does standard error name manager`. `RUN-22` constrains only the refusal message (`MUST write to
standard error a message naming the Seat — both, when both are`); `RUN-10` says of everything else
on that stream that `their wording is not specified`. So the item forbids a wording `RUN-10`
permits.

It is live: the Reviewer applied the same assertion to `CNF-30`'s Round-2 Runs on a scratch copy
and the reference executable went red on its own progress lines (`rloop: run 1 round 1:
implementer`). `CNF-29` passes today only because that Run is refused before any Round begins and
its one progress line happens not to carry a Seat word. An Implementation whose pre-pick progress
line names the Seats it is about to probe satisfies `RUN-22` exactly and fails `CNF-29`.

## What to change

Owner's choice, one of:

1. **Scope the check to the refusal line.** `CNF-29` asserts the absence of the Seat word in the
   refusal message only — the line that carries the quoted probe line — and the prose says so.
   No requirement changes.
2. **Ground it in a requirement.** Amend `RUN-22` to say the refusal message names no Seat that
   can answer, and keep the assertion on that message, not on the stream.

Either way the item must rest on a requirement, not on the reference executable's choice of
progress wording. Both variants keep `m4-both-named` red.

Fold in the two suggestions from the same review:

- `not_named` returns 1 when its assertion holds (the `&&` short-circuits to grep's status);
  make it return 0 on success like `names` does.
- `conformance/run`'s `CNF-23` block has the same `tr '\0' '\n' < "$(ls … | head -1)"` trap the
  Round closed for `CNF-24`: when no argv matches, bash prints `: No such file or directory` on the
  suite's stderr. Guard it the same way.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, every gate PASS.
- `CNF-29` stays red against an Implementation that names both Seats when only one is
  unavailable, and green against one whose progress lines name Seats (`F5`, demonstrate both).
- The prose of `CNF-29` and, under option 2, `RUN-22` say what is asserted and why.
